# Recreation Prompt

Recreate **Hawkins Rift Riders**, a portrait-first browser top-down survival collection adventure. Preserve the protected loop: joystick/keyboard free roam in a bounded world, grab a nearby item, carry it, directional attack/flash against pursuing enemies, earn score on kills, collect a 60-entry persistent index, lose one of three HP on contact, and restart after game over. Transform presentation into an 80s small-town sci-fi horror mystery with bike-riding teens, friendship bands, walkie/gadget clues, supernatural portal rings, synth dread, shadow monsters, neon lab/town scenery, and large mobile-safe CTAs. Use inline HTML/CSS/Canvas/JavaScript with procedural art and approved catalog fonts/audio.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
- genre: top-down free-roam arcade survival / collection adventure
- objective: move through a bounded world, collect nearby equipment, discover a 60-item index, strike pursuing enemies, and survive while score increases from defeated enemies
- input model: virtual joystick / pointer buttons on mobile, keyboard movement plus grab and attack on desktop
- core loop: spawn into world, roam, grab an item, attack enemies within directional arc, earn score, reveal collection entries, survive until HP is depleted
- fail/friction state: enemies contact the player, remove one of three hearts, and trigger game over at zero HP with restart/menu options

## Protected mechanics
- Preserve player speed/friction, world bounds, camera follow, enemy pursuit, spawn cadence, item cap, enemy cap, three-heart failure, score-on-kill, random item drops, collection persistence, and directional attack arc.
- Preserve touch zones for movement, grab, and attack; no global touch suppression.
- Preserve single-canvas render architecture and requestAnimationFrame loop.

## Safe transformation surfaces
HUD vocabulary, title/menu copy, audio catalog mapping, palette, procedural entity silhouettes, background motifs, collection names, fonts, mobile panel styling, particles, and feedback language are safe to transform because they do not alter collisions, scoring, input semantics, or state flow.
